entry.title: Why random shaking sorts mixed particles by size
entry.summary: Physicists revisit the puzzle of granular segregation. Random vibration plus a one-way asymmetry, where small grains can fall into gaps but large ones cannot, appears to be enough to produce order without any sorting decision.

entry.title: A mathematician proves that greedy algorithms are optimal for a surprising class of puzzles
entry.summary: The proof explains why discarding look-ahead, a seemingly reckless shortcut, gives exactly the best answer when the puzzle has a particular exchange structure. Outside that structure, the same shortcut fails badly.

entry.title: The geometry of crumpled paper follows a simple rule
entry.summary: When a sheet is crumpled again and again, the total length of its creases grows logarithmically. Researchers model each new crease as fragmenting existing facets, a rule that ignores the sheet's history beyond its current facets.
